tasks.what: Read a written slab in the sidecar, over a labelled tile grid
tasks.note:
BUILT. `render.slab_svg` draws one slab in plan over a tile grid with the coordinates on both axes and the origin ringed; `render.slab_legend` returns the same colouring as data so the picture and the list cannot disagree about which piece is which. Three endpoints -- `/api/slabs`, `/api/slabs/legend/<path>`, `/api/slabs/svg/<path>` -- and a Slabs tab, added through the seam `index.html` already documented: one button, one section, one row in `_ROUTES`.

**Every placement is its REAL footprint after rotation**, from `build.placed_bounds` -- not its nominal size -- so a two-cell piece reads as two cells and an off-grid prop reads as off-grid. That is the same distinction two `verify` checks were once wrong about, and drawing the nominal box would have made this view agree with a bug.

**It is not a substitute for pasting and the page says so.** It cannot show a mesh, what a rotation does to a face, or whether a run one cell thick reads as solid, which is what every probe in `tools/` exists for. It answers what is in the file and where -- the half a photograph is worst at, and the half that would have caught the verge bolsters as arithmetic rather than as a kit fault.

The list is scanned on first sight of the screen rather than on page load: this output directory holds 1,584 slabs and someone who came to build a town should not pay for walking them. Paths come from the server's own scan and go back through `resolve_in`, the same guard every other file endpoint uses.

tasks.what: A 3D layer on the slab screen, orbiting the four review faces
tasks.note:
The plan view is silent about HEIGHT, and height is what every roofscape defect here has been about: a roof floating half a tile over the wall head, a chimney a course too tall, a warehouse at 10 ft eaves. `slab_axon` extrudes each placement from `p.y` to `p.y + size_y` and draws three faces, with a height ruler in tiles so a course is countable off the picture.

**It orbits, and that is the design rather than a convenience.** A probe read from one angle is a probe that lies -- a rank of blades hides its own gaps from the front. A single fixed axonometric would reproduce, in a viewer built to prevent that failure, the exact failure it was built to prevent. `AXON_AZIMUTHS` is the same four faces `review.ps1 360` walks in game, and an azimuth that is not a quarter turn is REFUSED rather than rounded.

Its limit is stated on the page and in the docstring: it draws COLLIDERS, not meshes. `md_wall_1x1_diag_01` measures 1.0x2.0x1.0 and is a blade cutting the cell corner to corner; here it looks solid. Massing is answerable from this view, material and surface are not, and no probe in `tools/` is retired for it.

Found on first use, 2026-09-01: Forest Church's temple carries 108 upper-floor tiles on three levels inside what should be one volume (`church-one-volume`), and its 130-cell market square carries three stalls and a well (`market-feature-report`).

tasks.what: Deal grass variants per cell so the lawn stops reading as a tiled floor
tasks.note:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 on East Tradebourne and on `PROBE spooky forest`. The ground plane is the largest thing on a board by area and the least designed thing on it: 48,038 `Grass - Lush` plus 20,023 `Grass 1x1` is 17% of all placements in ONE material, and on Gallowsmere ground is 87% of 9,408 cells. Read from directly above, every 2x2 block boundary is a visible seam and the tiles can be counted -- the one thing a ground plane must not let you do.

The 2x2 fusion in `_lay_terrain` is NOT the cause and must not be reverted for this: the same seam shows between 1x1 tiles, and the fusion is a free asset saving. The fix is variance, not size.

The machinery already exists and is the reason this is cheap: `WallFamily.deal` hands out one of several interchangeable panels per cell, keyed on the cell with crc32 so a rebuild is byte-identical, and `walls.stem_of` is the test for 'these differ only by a trailing index'. The same rule applied to the ground roles adds NO assets and no geometry. Check the catalog actually ships siblings for the grass roles before promising it -- that is the one measurement missing.

MEASURED 2026-09-03, before any code, and it settles the open question the task was filed with. **There is exactly ONE 1x1 grass tile in the installed packs** -- `Grass 1x1`, no sibling by `walls.stem_of` and none by shape either. So the 1x1 path cannot be given variance and must not be promised it.

**The 2x2 path can, and it is free.** `Grass - Lush` and `Grass - Sparse` are both 2.0x0.5x2.0, both `folder=Nature`, both `group_tag=grassland` -- and `Grass - Sparse` is used ZERO times on any board today while `Grass - Lush` is placed 48,038 times on East Tradebourne. That is 70% of all grass on the map, in the one place a variant already exists and is going unused.

So the scope is the 2x2 block in `_lay_terrain` and nothing else. Keyed on the cell with crc32 so a rebuild stays byte-identical, which is the rule `WallFamily.deal` follows and the reason a mask like `TileMap.forest` had to be neutral bit-for-bit.

Also found and NOT in scope: the pack ships `Grassy Road`, `Grassy Road Corner`, `Grassy Road T` and `Grassy Road Crossroad`, all 2x2 `grassland`, all unused. That is a shipped answer to the staircase trail in `lane-clutter-hugs-a-wall`'s sibling finding -- a path family with real corner pieces -- but they are 2x2 against a 1-cell trail, so it needs its own probe rather than a guess.

SHIPPED 2026-09-03. East Tradebourne A/B, same command, feature off vs on: Grass - Lush 48,125 -> 23,945 and Grass - Sparse 0 -> 24,180, total placements unchanged at 391,819, nothing else moved. The 1x1 path and the single-variant field role are untouched on real data. Largest slab 23,738 -> 24,325 bytes against the 30,720 cap.

**And the brief was wrong about the hash, which is the finding worth keeping.** It asked for a plain zlib.crc32 keyed on the cell, because that is what WallFamily.deal does. crc32 is LINEAR over GF(2) and a tile grid is a linear input, so keyed on a bare cell it is perfectly balanced and visibly striped: over a 370x300 grid the split is 0.5000 while same-as-neighbour is 0.69 horizontal and 0.71 vertical against an ideal 0.50 -- and rows z=40 and z=41 come out BIT-IDENTICAL. Every other crc32 deal in build.py mixes in a building id or a quarter, so the lattice had never shown. Taking high bits or packing the ints is no better. build.cell_deal_key runs a second crc32 over the DECIMAL TEXT of the first, which is not linear: 0.4996 / 0.4990, no structure, still crc32 so cross-process determinism is unchanged. The test asserts the neighbour rate rather than the balance, because a count cannot see a stripe.

The selector is neither walls.stem_of (which reads the two grasses as unrelated) nor group_tag='grassland' (which also holds Grassy Road, an 8x8 foam and Tilled Earth, whose own tags are dirt/farm) -- it is the matches of the role's FIRST matching palette query. And the pass deals for every 2x2 block role rather than ground alone, which woke marsh_2x2: the palette had declared its three swamp blocks interchangeable since it was written while _lay_terrain laid variant 0 on every cell. A fen now deals 91/89/61.

NOT SEEN ON A BOARD yet. A 50/50 per-cell deal of two grass textures is uniform noise and may want clumping instead.

tasks.what: Stop lane clutter standing in the middle of the lane
tasks.note:

That is a prop in roughly one route cell in nine, and one of them is a HEDGE standing in a footpath. The STREET branch immediately below it does exactly what the lane comment promises -- `if not near(x, z, frozenset()): continue` -- and carries three sentences explaining why the rate has to be a share of that narrow set. tasks.what: WITHDRAWN: the bank was already built, and the review that filed this was wrong
tasks.note:
MEASURED 2026-09-02, and it corrects an assumption made twice in one session. Reading only the lowest tiles suggests the ground sits at 0.5 and the river is a sheet of water lying ON the lawn. It is not. Through the whole stack on `PROBE spooky forest`: land tops at 3.5 everywhere, water surface at 2.5, riverbed at 0.5, edge taper at 3.0. The channel IS cut -- a full tile below the bank and three tiles to the bed.

So depth is not the gap; the TRANSITION is. Turf meets water in one hard step over a depth that is already correct, which is why the river reads flat from above and only reads as a channel in section. One course of bank between the two is a local, bounded change that makes it read from every angle.

Filed instead of a general height field, deliberately. Terrain is laid one tile per cell at a single scalar `grade`; relief costs a whole tile per cell of rise over ~151,700 surface tiles on East Tradebourne, which is +20-38% on a 391,651-asset board whose largest chunk already sits at 77% of the byte cap -- and it puts `chunk_datum`, `anchor_on_a_whole_tile`, `shells_rest_on_their_floors` and the paste datum in play at once, each of which exists because it caught a shipped defect. If relief is wanted, try it at scene scale first.

WITHDRAWN 2026-09-03, one day after being filed, and the correction is the point. The review said 'the transition from turf to water is one hard step'. It is not: `_lay_terrain` already lays a one-cell shingle course along the waterline on soft ground (`role = "field_1x1"`), and `_lay_quays` rails the edge where STREET or PLAZA meets water. Read at native pixels on `PROBE spooky forest`, the far bank is grass, then a shingle course, then a faced drop, then water -- working, and reading as a shore.

The pale strips I took for bare gravel in the review figure ARE that shingle course doing its job. `build.py` even says so at the point it lays the map edge: 'shore course proved a one-cell transition works'. Filed from a screenshot without grepping for the feature first, which is the exact failure this project records under 'a feature can be correct and absent' -- run the other way round.

tasks.what: Audit the two other crc32 deals keyed on nothing but a cell
tasks.note:
FOUND 2026-09-03 while landing ground-variants-break-the-grid, and verified independently. zlib.crc32 is linear over GF(2), so keyed on a bare cell it is perfectly balanced and visibly striped -- 0.69 horizontal and 0.71 vertical same-as-neighbour against an ideal 0.50, with consecutive rows coming out bit-identical. build.cell_deal_key is the fix and is documented there.

Two sites still key on a bare lattice and were outside that brief.

build.py:209 -- the map border bite, which takes the digest's high bits and mods by 4. High bits measured WORSE than the plain digest on the horizontal axis (0.34). It has a 'no lone teeth' repair after it which may be masking the pattern, so look at the raggedness before and after the repair, not just the draw.

build.py:8422 -- _scatter's per-cell draw against a threshold. A threshold test on a striped field puts trees in stripes, and the canopy is the most-looked-at scatter on any board.

Both want the neighbour-rate measurement rather than a balance check, for the reason the first one taught: a count cannot see a stripe. Neither is known to be visible on a board yet -- measure, then look, then fix.

tasks.what: Look at the two-grass deal on a board; per-cell noise may want clumping
tasks.note:
The counts are settled and the code is shipped: East Tradebourne deals Grass - Lush 23,945 against Grass - Sparse 24,180 where it used to lay Lush 48,125 times, with total placements unchanged. What is NOT settled is whether it reads well, and this project's rule is that a look is not optional.

The specific worry, raised by the agent that built it and worth keeping: **a 50/50 per-cell deal is uniform noise.** It breaks the countable lattice, which was the defect, but it replaces it with static rather than with ground. Real turf clumps -- a patch of sparse grass is several cells across, not one. So the honest possibilities are that per-cell is right, that it wants a weighting other than 50/50, or that it wants clumping (value noise over the block grid, still keyed through cell_deal_key so it stays rebuild-stable).
